description.checks: FastImage works at all in an Expo app (the Expo example, on iOS, Android and the web): an image loads, a missing one fails, reload() after a failure, a bundled image, several sizes, preload, and the cache methods (on the web, that getCachePath isn't supported).

smoke-load.checks: A remote image loads: onLoad with its size, then onLoadEnd with ok: true and the same size.
smoke-load.steps: Loads the 200×200 photo of a pug in a blanket from the image server (a new url each run). Passes when onLoad gave 200×200 and onLoadEnd's result is { ok: true, width: 200, height: 200 }.
smoke-load.shows: The pug photo in a small square.

smoke-error.checks: A missing image fails: onError with a message, then onLoadEnd with ok: false and an error.
smoke-error.steps: Loads a url the image server answers with a 404. Passes when onError's error isn't empty and onLoadEnd's result is { ok: false, error } with an error that isn't empty.
smoke-error.shows: An empty gray square: the image never loads.

smoke-reload.checks: reload() on the ref loads an image again after its request failed.
smoke-reload.steps: Loads the pug photo from a url the image server answers with a 503 the first time and the image after. On onError, calls the ref's reload(). Passes on the onLoad that follows; a second onError, or a ref without reload(), fails.
smoke-reload.shows: The pug photo in a small square. A failure leaves an empty gray square.

smoke-bundled.checks: A bundled image (require()) loads, at the size of its file.
smoke-bundled.steps: Shows require('./images/logo.png'), the 1000×1000 React logo. Passes when onLoad's size is 1000×1000.
smoke-bundled.shows: The light blue React logo on a small gray square.

smoke-sizes.checks: A source of several sizes loads the one that fits the view: on iOS and Android the one closest to the view's size in pixels, on the web the smallest at least as wide (the browser picks it from a srcset).
smoke-sizes.steps: Gives a 96 dp view three sizes of a square from the image server: 100 px (red), 300 px (green) and 900 px (blue). Passes when onLoad's width is the size expected for the screen's pixel ratio: 300 px on the test phones (3× on iOS, 2.625× on Android) and on the web (its page is at 3×).
smoke-sizes.shows: A solid green square, larger than the other rows' images. Red or blue means the wrong size was loaded.

smoke-preload.checks: FastImage.preload resolves with a result per source: ok with the size for an image that loads, not ok for a missing one.
smoke-preload.steps: Preloads a 120×120 photo and a url the image server answers with a 404, when it mounts. Passes when the first result is { ok: true, width: 120, height: 120 } and the second isn't ok.
smoke-preload.shows: An empty gray square: the images are only preloaded, not shown.

smoke-cache-path.checks: FastImage.getCachePath gives the file of an image a view has loaded.
smoke-cache-path.steps: Loads a 120×120 photo of the northern lights; on onLoad, calls FastImage.getCachePath with the same source. Passes when the result is ok with a path.
smoke-cache-path.shows: The northern lights photo (green sky over a dark tree) in a small square.

smoke-cache-limits.checks: FastImage.configureCache() reports the cache limits the app's config sets with FastImage's Expo config plugin.
smoke-cache-limits.steps: Calls FastImage.configureCache() without changes when it mounts. Passes when it reports maxDiskSize 150 MB, maxDiskAge 7 days and maxMemorySize 50 MB, as in app.config.js.
smoke-cache-limits.shows: An empty gray square: nothing loads here.

description.checks: #436: a FastImage's open sides follow the loaded image, as an 's do: the other side from its aspect ratio, or its own size with neither set.

auto-size-width.checks: An image with only a width (in a row) gets the height its aspect ratio gives.
auto-size-width.steps: Loads a 600x300 photo with style { width: 240, height: 'auto' } in a row. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 240x120.
auto-size-width.shows: The photo at 240x120 on the left, not stretched.

auto-size-height.checks: An image with only a height (in a row) gets the width its aspect ratio gives.
auto-size-height.steps: Loads the 600x300 photo with style { width: 'auto', height: 64 } in a row. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 128x64.
auto-size-height.shows: The photo at 128x64 on the left.

auto-size-natural.checks: An image with no size (in a row) is its own size: a 120x120 image is 120x120 points.
auto-size-natural.steps: Loads a 120x120 photo with style { width: 'auto', height: 'auto' } in a row. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 120x120.
auto-size-natural.shows: The 120x120 photo at 120x120 points on the left.

auto-size-left-out.checks: Opt-in: a side the style leaves out (rather than setting to 'auto') doesn't follow the image, and stays 0, as with React Native's Image.
auto-size-left-out.steps: Loads the 600x300 photo with style { width: 240 } in a row. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 240x0.

auto-size-scale.checks: A bundled @3x image with no size is its size in points: its pixels over its file's scale.
auto-size-scale.steps: Shows require('./images/center-dot.png'), only a 120x120 @3x file, with no style in a row. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 40x40.
auto-size-scale.shows: A 40x40 blue square on the left.

description.checks: #436, continued: an SVG's own size, a FastImageBackground's image, and how an image with only a width is decoded and shown as it loads.

auto-size-svg.checks: An SVG with no size is its own size: a 24x24 SVG is 24x24 points.
auto-size-svg.steps: Loads a 24x24 SVG of a black ring with style { width: 'auto', height: 'auto' } in a row. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 24x24.
auto-size-svg.shows: A 24x24 black ring on the left.

auto-size-background.checks: A FastImageBackground's image fills it: its insets (absoluteFill) set its size, which doesn't follow the image.
auto-size-background.steps: Shows the 600x300 photo in a 160x160 FastImageBackground. Passes once it has loaded and the image is 160x160.
auto-size-background.shows: The photo covering a 160x160 square (its middle).

auto-size-downsample.checks: An image with only a width is decoded for its size, as one with both sides set is: they look the same.
auto-size-downsample.steps: Loads a 1600x1000 page of text at 128x80, and again (another url) with only a width of 128, which follows the image to 128x80. Passes once both have loaded.
auto-size-downsample.shows: The same text page twice, at 128x80, with the same sharpness. A blurrier or more aliased right one means it was decoded at another size.

auto-size-cover.checks: An image with only a width and objectFit cover shows the whole image as it loads, not a crop of its middle for a size the view doesn't get.
auto-size-cover.steps: Records the left quarter of a 240x120 box, then loads a 600x300 image of magenta, cyan and magenta thirds into it with style { width: 240, height: 'auto' }, until 1.5 s after onLoad. Passes when the recording sees magenta, and never cyan.
auto-size-cover.shows: The image at 240x120: magenta, cyan and magenta thirds.

description.checks: #436, continued: padding, borders, and a later style's height: 'auto'.

auto-size-padding.checks: With padding, the image (which fills the view, padding included) has its aspect ratio: the padding isn't added to it.
auto-size-padding.steps: Loads the 600x300 photo with style { width: 96, height: 'auto', padding: 8 } in a row. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 96x48.
auto-size-padding.shows: The photo at 96x48 on the left.

auto-size-padding-natural.checks: With padding and neither side set, the view is the image's own size: the image fills it, padding included.
auto-size-padding-natural.steps: Loads a 120x120 photo with style { width: 'auto', height: 'auto', padding: 20 } in a row. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 120x120.
auto-size-padding-natural.shows: The 120x120 photo at 120x120 points on the left.

auto-size-border.checks: With borders, the image (inside them) has its aspect ratio: the borders aren't part of it.
auto-size-border.steps: Loads the 600x300 photo with style { width: 240, height: 'auto', borderWidth: 8 } in a row. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 240x128 (the image 224x112).
auto-size-border.shows: The photo at 224x112 inside an 8-point black border, on the left.

auto-size-cleared.checks: A height of 'auto' in a later style replaces an earlier style's height.
auto-size-cleared.steps: Loads the 600x300 photo with style [{ height: 200 }, { width: 96, height: 'auto' }] in a row. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 96x48.
auto-size-cleared.shows: The photo at 96x48 on the left.

auto-size-padding-cover.checks: An image with only a width, padding and objectFit cover shows the whole image as it loads, not a crop of it for the padding's strip.
auto-size-padding-cover.steps: Records the point 10 points below the top of a 240x128 box, then loads a 600x300 image whose top fifth is magenta and the rest cyan into it with style { width: 240, height: 'auto', padding: 8 }, until 1.5 s after onLoad. Passes when the recording sees magenta, and never cyan.
auto-size-padding-cover.shows: The image at 240x120: a magenta band at the top over cyan.

auto-size-padding-tall.checks: An image with only a width and padding taller than the image's shape gives it shows once it has loaded, though the view is 0 high inside its padding.
auto-size-padding-tall.steps: Records the point 10 points below the top of a 240x144 box, then loads a 600x300 image whose top fifth is magenta and the rest cyan into it with style { width: 240, height: 'auto', padding: 70 } (240x140), until 1.5 s after onLoad. Passes when the recording sees magenta, and never cyan.
auto-size-padding-tall.shows: The image at 240x140, cover: a magenta band at the top over cyan.

description.checks: #436, continued: the style's aspectRatio with neither side set, and a height that grows from about 0.

auto-size-aspect-ratio.checks: The style's aspectRatio wins over the image's, also with neither side set: the image's width (at most the space there is), and the height from the style's ratio.
auto-size-aspect-ratio.steps: Loads the 600x300 photo with style { width: 'auto', aspectRatio: 1 } in a 120-point-wide row. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 120x120.
auto-size-aspect-ratio.shows: The photo stretched to a 120x120 square on the left.

auto-size-aspect-ratio-column.checks: As auto-size-aspect-ratio, in a column with alignItems center, where the width isn't stretched.
auto-size-aspect-ratio-column.steps: Loads the 600x300 photo with style { width: 'auto', aspectRatio: 1 } in a 120-point-wide column with alignItems center. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 120x120.
auto-size-aspect-ratio-column.shows: The photo stretched to a 120x120 square on the left.

auto-size-grow.checks: An image with both sides set and objectFit contain, whose height grows from about 0 once it has loaded, is decoded again for its new size, not left as the copy decoded for the first one.
auto-size-grow.steps: Loads a 1024x1024 photo with style { width: 120, height: 1 / PixelRatio.get() } (a box 1 pixel high) and objectFit contain, and 300 ms after onLoad makes the height 120. Passes 1.5 s later; the screenshot shows whether it was decoded again.
auto-size-grow.shows: The photo at 120x120, sharp. A flat color (one pixel stretched) means it kept the copy decoded for the first size.

description.checks: #436, continued: a source's own size: several sources' scale, and a single source's width and height, laid out before the image loads.

auto-size-sources-scale.checks: Of several sources, the picked one's pixels over its scale are its size in points, as a bundled @2x or @3x image's are.
auto-size-sources-scale.steps: Shows two sources of a 200x200 photo, each { width: 80, height: 80, scale: 2.5 }, with style { width: 'auto', height: 'auto' } in a row. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 80x80.
auto-size-sources-scale.shows: The photo at 80x80 on the left.

auto-size-source-width.checks: A single source's width and height are its size in points, as with React Native's Image, also with no style: a 120x120 image given as 64x64 is 64x64.
auto-size-source-width.steps: Loads a 120x120 photo as { uri, width: 64, height: 64 } with no style in a row. Passes once it has loaded and its layout is 64x64.
auto-size-source-width.shows: The photo at 64x64 on the left.

auto-size-declared.checks: A single source's width and height lay the view out before the image loads, so its layout doesn't change when it does.
auto-size-declared.steps: Loads the 600x300 photo (on iOS and Android from a download that takes 2 s) as { uri, width: 128, height: 64 } with no style in a row. Passes once it has loaded if every layout, at least one of them before onLoad, was 128x64.
auto-size-declared.shows: The photo at 128x64 on the left.

description.checks: #436, continued: a url placeholder, several sizes, a source change and a failed one, of an image with only a width, and a source change of one with neither side set.

auto-size-placeholder.checks: A url placeholder of an image with only a width is decoded for that width, so another view showing the same placeholder shows it whole.
auto-size-placeholder.steps: Shows a photo the slow server sends over about 35 s, with style { width: 240, height: 'auto' } and a placeholder url of a 600x300 image of magenta, cyan and magenta thirds. 2.5 s later, a 128x64 view with another slow photo and the same placeholder mounts. Passes then.
auto-size-placeholder.shows: The thirds at 128x64: magenta, cyan and magenta. A single smeared color means the placeholder was decoded 1 pixel high.

auto-size-source-change.checks: An image with only a width and objectFit cover whose source changes to an image of another shape shows the whole new image, not a crop of it for the previous image's shape.
auto-size-source-change.steps: Loads a 120x120 photo with style { width: 240, height: 'auto' } (240x240), then records the point 8 points below the view's top while the source changes to a 600x300 image whose top fifth is magenta and the rest cyan, until 1.5 s after its onLoad. Passes when the recording sees magenta, and never cyan.
auto-size-source-change.shows: The 600x300 image at 240x120: a magenta band at the top over cyan.

auto-size-natural-change.checks: An image with neither side set and objectFit cover whose source changes to an image of another shape shows the whole new image, not a crop of it for the previous image's shape.
auto-size-natural-change.steps: Loads a 120x120 photo with style { width: 'auto', height: 'auto' } in a 240-wide row (120x120), then records a point right of the view's middle, outside the first photo, while the source changes to a 600x300 image of magenta, cyan and magenta thirds (240x120, the row's width), until 1.5 s after its onLoad. Passes when the recording sees magenta, and never cyan.
auto-size-natural-change.shows: The thirds at 240x120: magenta, cyan and magenta.

auto-size-sources.checks: With several sizes of an image and only a width, the size for that width loads, and only that one.
auto-size-sources.steps: Loads a 256x256 and a 1024x1024 size of a photo as source, with style { width: 64, height: 'auto' } in a row. Passes when, 2 s after onLoad, the server got one request for the 256 px one and none for the 1024 px one.
auto-size-sources.shows: The photo at 64x64 on the left.

auto-size-failed.checks: An image with only a width whose source changes to one that fails is 0 high again, as before an image loaded, not the previous image's height.
auto-size-failed.steps: Loads the 600x300 photo with style { width: 96, height: 'auto' } in a row (96x48), then changes the source to a url that 404s. Passes when, 1 s after onError, its layout is 96x0.

description.checks: Features that on Android go through the Glide components FastImage registers itself when the app's AppGlideModule is expo-image's: onProgress, cache: 'web', writeToCache, SVG and APNG images. iOS runs the same cases.

smoke-progress.checks: onProgress comes while a remote image downloads, the last one with all of it loaded, before onLoad. On Android in an app with expo-image, it goes through the Glide components FastImage registers itself.
smoke-progress.steps: Loads the pug photo from the image server with onProgress. Passes on onLoad if the last onProgress had loaded equal to total.
smoke-progress.shows: The pug photo in a small square.

smoke-web-cache.checks: A source with cache: 'web' uses the HTTP cache: loaded twice from a url the server marks as cacheable, it's requested once.
smoke-web-cache.steps: Loads the pug photo with cache: 'web' from a url the image server sends with Cache-Control: max-age=3600, then mounts a new view for it once it has loaded. After the second onLoad, removes the view and asks the image server how many times the url was requested; passes on 1.
smoke-web-cache.shows: An empty gray square: the image view is gone after the second load.

smoke-write-to-cache.checks: FastImage.writeToCache stores a file as a url's image, which a view then shows from the cache without downloading it.
smoke-write-to-cache.steps: Downloads a 120×120 photo of the northern lights with FastImage.getCachePath, then calls FastImage.writeToCache with the pug photo's url and that file. Then shows the pug url with cache: 'cacheOnly'; passes when onLoad's width is 120 (the stored file, not the 200×200 pug).
smoke-write-to-cache.shows: The northern lights photo (green sky over a dark tree) in a small square. The pug, or an empty gray square, is a failure.

smoke-svg.checks: An SVG image from a url loads. expo-image brings the SVG libraries into this app too, so this doesn't check that FastImage includes them (the main example does).
smoke-svg.steps: Loads a 24×24 SVG of a black ring from the image server. Passes on onLoad.
smoke-svg.shows: A thick black ring on a small gray square.

smoke-apng.steps: Loads an APNG of two frames, red then blue, 400 ms each and looping. On onLoad, records the image for 1.6 s (two plays). Passes when the recording sees both red and blue.
smoke-apng.shows: A red or blue square (animated, so it's not compared). The recording sees red and blue in turn.

smoke-apng-blur.checks: An animated PNG (APNG) with blurRadius shows its first frame, blurred and still. On Android in an app with expo-image, Glide also has APNG4Android's plugin for APNGs, which ignores Glide's "don't animate" option.
smoke-apng-blur.steps: Loads an APNG of two frames, red then blue, 400 ms each and looping, with blurRadius 4. On onLoad, records the image for 1.6 s (two plays). Passes when the recording sees red only.
smoke-apng-blur.shows: A red square (animated images are masked, so it's not compared). The recording sees red only; never blue.

description.checks: expo-image works next to FastImage in the same app.

expo-image.checks: expo-image's Image loads in the same app as FastImage. On Android both use Glide, and the app's AppGlideModule is expo-image's (FastImage leaves its own out), so expo-image keeps its own setup.
expo-image.steps: Loads a 120×120 photo of a bear on rocks from the image server with expo-image's Image (a new url each run). Passes on onLoad; onError fails.
expo-image.shows: The bear photo in a small square.
